title: What Is an Aortic Dissection?
hook: A tear in the wall of the body's largest artery — the emergency behind Sen. Lindsey Graham's death — can go from first symptom to fatal in minutes. Here's what it is and why speed matters.
key_points: An aortic dissection is a tear in the inner wall of the aorta, the body's main artery.
Blood forces its way between the artery's layers, weakening or rupturing it.
The hallmark symptom is sudden, severe chest or back pain, often described as tearing or ripping.
High blood pressure and connective-tissue disorders are the leading risk factors.
It's a medical emergency — survival depends on rapid diagnosis and treatment.
content_html: An aortic dissection made headlines as the preliminary finding behind Sen. Lindsey Graham's death — and it's the kind of medical emergency that can go from first symptom to fatal in a very short window. NPR's A Martínez spoke with Dr. Manesh Patel, volunteer president of the American Heart Association, about what it actually is.
extra_html:
The aorta is the body's largest artery, carrying blood straight from the heart. Its wall is built in layers, and a dissection happens when the inner layer tears, letting blood surge into the space between the layers instead of staying inside the vessel. That can weaken the aorta enough to rupture, or block blood flow to organs the aorta feeds along its length.

The warning sign is usually unmistakable: sudden, severe chest or back pain that people often describe as tearing or ripping — very different from the gradual chest tightness associated with a heart attack. High blood pressure is the biggest risk factor, since it puts constant stress on the artery wall; some connective-tissue disorders raise risk too. Because a dissection can turn fatal within minutes to hours, it's treated as a "call 911 now" emergency, not a symptom to sleep on.

flashcards.prompt: What actually happens to the artery in an aortic dissection?
flashcards.back_html: The inner wall of the aorta tears, letting blood force its way between the artery's layers — weakening the vessel and risking rupture.

flashcards.prompt: What's the classic warning symptom of an aortic dissection?

choices.text: Sudden, severe chest or back pain described as tearing or ripping
A gradual, dull ache that builds over several weeks
Painless shortness of breath only during exercise

flashcards.explanation_html: Aortic dissection typically announces itself abruptly — sudden, severe pain in the chest or back, often described as a tearing or ripping sensation, not a slow build-up.

flashcards.prompt: Why is an aortic dissection treated as a medical emergency?
flashcards.back_html: Once the artery wall tears, it can rupture within minutes to hours. Survival depends on getting diagnosed and treated fast — this isn't a wait-and-see condition.
